title: Entity State Flapping Detector
dataSources: Home Assistant state/logbook events (`homeassistant:event`), Homey flow/insights (`homey:flow`), SmartThings events (`smartthings:event`), Hubitat/openHAB logs, Node-RED flow events (`nodered:event`).
app: Home Assistant / Homey / SmartThings / Hubitat / openHAB event streams via MQTT, webhooks, and REST - forwarded to Splunk HEC.
spl:
index=personal sourcetype=homeassistant:event event_type=state_changed
| bin _time span=1h
| stats dc(new_state) as distinct_states, count as events by entity_id _time
| where events>10 AND distinct_states>2
| sort - events
description: Finds sensors and entities that are bouncing between states far too often, a classic sign of noisy hardware, bad thresholds, or chatty integrations.
value: Flapping makes automations brittle and dashboards noisy; catching the culprit entity is much easier than debugging the downstream chaos it causes.
implementation: Forward state-change events with entity identifiers; alert on hourly flap storms before they break dependent automations.
visualization: Hourly table of entities by change count and distinct states.
grandmaExplanation: It spots when one device keeps changing its mind over and over and starts confusing the rest of the smart home.
